Why the VMM-read P2 efficiency is not 96% — run_46 autopsy

One nominal sub_run taken apart event by event: every alternative explanation excluded by measurement, and the VMM discriminator threshold left as the only one.

Analysis 2026-08-16 micromegas,vmm,sps,efficiency,threshold

The answer. It is the VMM discriminator threshold, and nothing else. The threshold sits at roughly the most probable signal, so a few per cent of gain moves the efficiency by ten points — and the pads that happen to see the largest pulses already measure 96.2%, the DREAM number, on the same plane in the same run. Every other explanation is excluded below by measurement, not by argument.

The run, and what it is being compared to

run_46/cfg_gain4.5_peaktime200, 2026-08-01: mesh 450 V, drift 750 V on all three stations — the nominal operating point, the same HV as run_36/operating_* and run_32/meshscan_m00V — with the best VMM configuration of the campaign (gain 4.5 mV/fC, peaking time 200 ns). It is the highest P2_OUT efficiency measured anywhere in the campaign, so a deficit found here is a floor on the problem, not a badly chosen working point. 837,338 uRWELL tracks carry a matched VMM trigger time, over 48 captures and 1.52 × 109 VMM hits.

The reference is highstat_eff_1/beam_commissioning_00, 2026-07-25: the same detectors read out by DREAM, the same gas, the same mesh voltage, the same uRWELL tracks, the same analysis and the same cuts.

stationDREAM readoutVMM readout (run_46)
P2_IN0.96490.155
P2_MID0.97060.669
P2_OUT0.96040.854

P2_MID and P2_OUT are the same physical detectors on both dates. P2_IN is not necessarily — a detector was swapped on 27 July — so its two numbers are not strictly the same object, and it is treated separately throughout.

What it is not

Each of these is a measurement.

Not tracks counted outside the active area

All 837,338 tracks land within 9 mm of an instrumented pad. The projected beam is a ~110 × 110 mm patch covering 69–73 pads in the middle of the 384-pad instrumented region, nowhere near its edge. The identical fiducial definition gives DREAM 96%.

Not the geometry or the channel map (on P2_MID and P2_OUT)

The uRWELL → pad transform is a proper −59.98° rotation with unit singular values, and the residual is 3.37 / 3.44 mm = 12 mm/√12 — the pad quantisation, i.e. the pointing is as good as pads allow. Better than that: the VMM finds the same dead pad as DREAM. Pad 635 (VMM 17 channel 4) at (411, 237) mm reads 29.8% here, and is the same dark square at (410, 237) in the DREAM map. Two completely different electronics chains, same defect, same coordinates.

Not the coincidence window

Widening it from 3σ to 20σ moves P2_OUT from 0.8540 to 0.8579. For the tracks that miss, the hits within 15 mm of the prediction are flat across ±10 µs at the accidental level (~72 per 250 ns bin): there is no out-of-time signal being cut away.

Not position matching or clustering

The efficiency asks for any pad within 15 mm, and it plateaus by 8 mm (0.8496 at 8 mm, 0.8567 at 40 mm). For 95.7% of the misses there is nothing within 15 mm at any time in ±10 µs — the pad simply did not fire.

Not rate, dead time or pile-up

P2_OUT efficiency sliced byrange over the slices
time into the spill, 0 → 6 s0.855 … 0.856
triggers within ±1 ms, 0 → 120.853 … 0.856
time since the previous trigger, <10 µs → >1 ms0.851 … 0.855
uRWELL front–back agreement |dx|, 0 → 3 mm0.83 … 0.88, no trend

Flat everywhere. And VMM 19, whose channel 20 runs at 116 kHz, is the second most efficient chip of P2_OUT at 86.2% — a screaming channel does not blind the chip it sits on.

Not missing captures, pad-boundary charge sharing, or a common-mode DAQ loss

Capture coverage is 100% of the tracks. Folding every pad onto one cell, the efficiency is flat across it — 0.85 at the centre, 0.81 at 7.5 mm out — so charge splitting between pads is not where it goes. And P2_MID and P2_OUT miss almost independently: both fire on 52.1% of tracks against 50.5% predicted by independence, so whole events are not being dropped somewhere common.

What it is

The pulse-height spectrum of the hits that are found is a Landau chopped off at its low side. On P2_OUT the lowest ADC seen is 47, the 5th percentile is 81 and the most probable value is 128: the spectrum does not rise from zero, it starts at a wall. Efficiency is correspondingly steep right there — adding 50 ADC counts offline costs 14 points (0.854 → 0.715), adding 100 costs 41 points.

Five things that move the efficiency, all of them electronics

1. The amplifier gain, which cannot change a detector. run_41 (3.0 mV/fC) and run_48 (4.5 mV/fC), same HV, same gas, the same threshold DAC on five of the six P2_OUT chips, 4½ hours apart: P2_OUT 0.723 → 0.822.

2. The threshold DAC alone. run_47 and run_48 are the same configuration file with every per-chip sdt line commented out or set — identical gain, peaking time, HV, gas and beam, 36 minutes apart.

P2_INP2_MIDP2_OUT
_deflt (base thresholds)0.0490.2180.486
_opt (tuned per chip)0.1670.5980.822

3. Which chip you are on. Within P2_MID, at one instant, VMM 9 and VMM 12 sit at sdt 256 and read 0.53 and 0.31; VMM 10, 11 and 13 sit at sdt 224 and read 0.78, 0.70 and 0.72.

4. Where that DAC lands on each chip's own signal. All five illuminated P2_OUT chips are at sdt 224 and they read 0.897, 0.862, 0.844, 0.829 and 0.763 — a 13-point spread at one threshold setting, with pulse-height medians running from 119 to 162 ADC. The VMM's per-channel trim DACs were never used, so one global threshold per chip means the effective threshold moves with every channel's baseline.

5. Pad by pad, efficiency tracks pulse height. Over the 69 illuminated pads of P2_OUT the correlation between a pad's median pulse height and its efficiency is +0.55 (P2_MID: +0.52 over 54 pads):

pad median pulse height [ADC]efficiencytracks
90–1270.752151,914
127–1390.816241,640
139–1680.892163,012
168–2020.920174,252
202–2710.921106,159

Note the direction. If this were a selection effect it would run the other way: a channel with a high threshold records only its big pulses, so it would show a high median with a low efficiency. The observed correlation is positive, so it is real signal-size variation and it dominates. The best individual pads reach 0.962, 0.957, 0.954; DREAM measured 0.9604. A detector cannot be 96% efficient on some pads and 60% on others under one uniform beam. A readout with one global threshold per chip and no per-channel trim can.

The mesh scan and the amplifier-gain step are one curve

If the readout is threshold-limited then the mesh-HV scan is not a detector curve at all: it is the survival function of the signal-charge distribution swept past a fixed threshold. Fitting a Landau survival to the 11-point mesh scan (0.734 at nominal down to 0.0078 at −100 V) and requiring it to pass through the ×1.5 amplifier-gain point — a gain change of exactly known size, on a different physical knob — returns a gain e-folding of V0 = 22.4 V, which is what a bulk Micromegas has, and which was not an input to the fit. The discriminator comes out at 0.68 × the most probable signal.

Read the table where the scan measured it. The model's asymptote is an artefact of the Landau's unphysical low tail — and what the detector can do at this HV is not a model question anyway, since DREAM measured it.

Two bugs in the analysis, found on the way

The hot-channel mask was deleting beam. It flagged any channel above 8× its own chip's median occupancy. On a chip whose threshold has been raised the noise disappears, the median collapses, and the illuminated pads stand 30–50× above it — so they get masked. On P2_MID this removed 64,630 hits arriving exactly at the +115 ns trigger latency. The pads it killed measure 61% efficiency with the mask off and 1% with it on: VMM 9 was never dead, it was masked.

Flagging on the out-of-time occupancy instead does not fix it — the beam delivers particles at tens of kHz while the matched trigger runs at ~1.4 kHz, so most of a beam pad's hits are out of time with a matched trigger. The rule is now an absolute rate: a 12 × 12 mm pad in this beam takes a few kHz, the pathological channels sit at 105 Hz, and there are two decades of clear air between them.

stationratio rule (as published)absolute rate (corrected)
P2_IN0.15350.1552
P2_MID0.59160.6688
P2_OUT0.85400.8540

P2_OUT is untouched, so the headline number stands. The rule also still does its job where it matters: leaving VMM 4 channel 39 (460 kHz) in inflates P2_IN to 0.2253 by pure accidental coincidence, since at that rate the channel fires in 29% of the 630 ns windows all by itself.

The second bug: a few hits per capture carry srs_timestamp = 0, so taking each capture's span as (min, max) of its hit times stretched every one of them back to zero. Unioned, that made the "was the VMM recording" cut accept everything, and made the live time come out 25× too long. Both now use quantiles.

The three stations

What to do about it

  1. Use the VMM's per-channel threshold trim. Only one global sdt per chip was ever set. The per-pad efficiency spread of 0.59–0.96 at a single DAC value is what that costs.
  2. Get the global thresholds down. sdt 224–230 is not a low threshold here: it is 0.68 × the most probable signal.
  3. Fix the noisy channels at source (VMM 4 ch 39, VMM 19 ch 20) instead of raising the whole chip's threshold to hide them — that trade cost the entire chip on P2_IN.
  4. Bench-check VMM 12 of P2_MID (27 dead channels), and re-derive the P2_IN channel → pad map, now that uRWELL tracks make a proper derivation possible.

Code and the full numeric report: sps_beam_analysis/vmm_dream_matching/ in P2_basket_analysis — eff_autopsy.py, eff_autopsy_report.py, gain_threshold_model.py, and EFFICIENCY_AUTOPSY.md. The campaign table is being re-measured with the corrected mask.
